_about: Public-domain William Parkinson, pastor of the First Baptist Church in the City of New York, for the Word Hoard: a sermon of 1812, his Jubilee sermon with a history of that church, and a sermon in his series on Deuteronomy xxxiii. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 127 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

parkinson-sermon-1812: A sermon, delivered in the meeting house of the First Baptist church in the city of New York, August 20th, 1812. Being a day recommended, by the constituted authorities of the nation, as a day of special humiliation and prayer, on account of the present war (New-York, Printed for J. Tiebout, 1812)
parkinson-jubilee: Jubilee : a sermon, containing a history of the origin of the First Baptist Church in the City of New York, and its progress, during the first fifty years since its constitution (with explanatory notes) : delivered in the meeting-house of said church, Jan. 1, 1813 (New-York : Printed for the proprietor, 1813)
parkinson-deuteronomy: A sermon; being one of a series of sermons on the XXXIII chapter of Deuteronomy ([New York], 1828)
